cards.front: Operative treatment indications for pediatric both bone forearm fractures following unsuccessful closed reduction : Children < 10 y/o: Angulation >15°, rotation >45° Children ≥ 10 y/o: Angulation >10°, rotation >30°, bayonet apposition
cards.extra: 13 y/o is cutoff. After that age they are too close to skeletal maturity and should be treated like adults. Nooonan and Price (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9689186/) provide guidelines for acceptable displacement of the radius and ulna. In fractures in any level in children less than 9 years of age, complete displacement, 15 degrees of angulation, and 45 degrees of malrotation are acceptable. In children age 9 or older, 30 degrees of malrotation is acceptable, with 10 degrees of angulation for proximal fractures and 15 degrees for more distal fractures. Complete bayonet apposition is acceptable as long as angulation does not exceed 20 degrees and the patient has at least 2 years of growth remaining.
